name: Expertise
description: You gain Expertise (double proficiency bonus) in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Sleight of Hand and Stealth are recommended if you have proficiency in them.

name: Sneak Attack
description: Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or Ranged weapon. You don't need Advantage if an ally is within 5 feet of the target, the ally isn't Incapacitated, and you don't have Disadvantage on the roll.

descriptions.3: Once per turn, you can deal an extra 2d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or Ranged weapon. You don't need Advantage if an ally is within 5 feet of the target, the ally isn't Incapacitated, and you don't have Disadvantage on the roll.

name: Thieves' Cant
description: You know Thieves' Cant — the secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code of the criminal underworld — and one other language of your choice.

name: Weapon Mastery
description: Your training allows you to use the mastery properties of 2 kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Daggers and Shortbows. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change those weapon choices. See Weapon Mastery cards for property details.

name: Cunning Action
description: On your turn, take Dash, Disengage, or Hide as a Bonus Action.

name: Steady Aim
description: As a Bonus Action, gain Advantage on your next attack roll this turn. You must not have moved this turn; your Speed becomes 0 until the end of the turn.

name: Fast Hands
description: As a Bonus Action, make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check to pick a lock or disarm a trap with Thieves' Tools, or pick a pocket. Alternatively, take the Utilize action or the Magic action to use a magic item that requires it.

name: Second-Story Work
description: Gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed. You can use Dexterity instead of Strength to determine your jump distance.
